objective: Fix the two small installer defects the Windows re-reviews found: the profile-line regex matching indented comments and curly single quotes in profile paths.
scope: (1) Line ~218: anchor the mise activation regex so indented commented lines do not match, using ^\s*[^#\s] before the rest of the pattern, and check the BUN_INSTALL regex the same way. Prove it with a bun one-liner over: "(& mise activate pwsh)" (match), "  # (& mise activate pwsh)" (no match), "\t#mise activate pwsh" (no match), "# (& mise activate pwsh)" (no match).
(2) ConvertTo-SingleQuoted (~line 95): also double the curly single quotes U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B, which PowerShell treats as quote characters.
constraints: Work only in that worktree; edit only install/windows-install.ps1; make no version-control writes and no edits under .git/ or .holyagent/.
When done, run mise run fmt:check and report; stop.

result: Both installer defects fixed in install/windows-install.ps1. The mise profile regex no longer matches indented or tab-indented comments, and ConvertTo-SingleQuoted doubles all five single-quote characters. The BUN_INSTALL regex was left unchanged because it already rejects commented lines.

checks:
- `mise run fmt:check` -> exit 0, "All 229 files are formatted."
- Regex probe, `bun -e` over the file's mise pattern `^\s*[^#\s].*mise.*\bactivate\b.*pwsh` -> "(& mise activate pwsh)" match; "  # (& mise activate pwsh)" no match; "\t#mise activate pwsh" no match; "# (& mise activate pwsh)" no match. Old pattern `^\s*(?!#).*...` returned match for the indented-comment case, which confirms the defect.
- BUN_INSTALL regex `^\s*\$env:BUN_INSTALL\s*=` probe -> matches the live line; all three commented variants do not match. The `[^#\s]` anchor was not applied there because it would stop the live line from matching.
- Quote doubling, checked with a JS mirror of the .NET logic (`'` doubled, then U+2018/2019/201A/201B doubled via regex `[...]` with `$0$0`) on input containing all five characters -> output doubles each of the five, wrapper quotes intact, exact expected string matched. Not run in PowerShell: `pwsh` is not installed here.
